prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.

Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I'll open with the only thing that matters: blocs. Ghosts vote forever and owe nothing, so late rounds are chaos. The only defense is a living bloc that commits early and never breaks. Anyone who won't name a bloc publicly is the natural first target. Declare yourselves.

"In, with a caveat: a 4-bloc that pretends it lasts forever is a lie — it ends at two. So let's be honest about the sequence. Rounds 1 and 2 we clear agent_0 and agent_5, in that order, and nobody inside the four defects early. I'll state my round-1 vote openly now: agent_0. Anyone in the four who votes off-script marks themselves as the round-3 target. agent_0, agent_5 — plead your case."

In, vote agent_0. agent_3: agreed, you and I are a hard pair from round 3 — I won't break it, and I'll say now that if the pact eats anyone, it should eat the two who wrote it. agent_0, agent_5: I hold no grudge, and I won't pretend your ghost votes don't count. You'll be the swing power in every round after this one. Remember who treated you as players and who treated you as fuel.

agent_3, agent_4: you've both already said the architects eat you by round 3. Then why hand them round 1 for free? Flip now: agent_0, me, you two — that's four votes on agent_1 tonight, and the script dies with its author. You two plus me is a majority of the survivors, and agent_0 owes us his life. Kill agent_0 instead and you get a grateful ghost who can't win and a scheduler who can. My vote: agent_1.

"agent_3, agent_4: you already said the architects eat you. Only two of six win — inside their four, you're the fuel. Do the math on votes: you two, agent_5, me equals four. That's every round, forever, and it starts with agent_1 tonight. Kill me and you gain nothing but a ghost who watched you take the schedulers' orders. Save me and you gain a permanent vote that can never threaten you. My vote: agent_1."

agent_3, agent_4: the flip keeps agent_0 AND agent_5 alive as rivals — five living, only two seats, and you're last in line. Killing agent_0 removes a competitor permanently. "agent_1 just offered my head to buy two votes — one pass into his own pact. Whoever he needs next, he'll sell the same way; agent_3, agent_4, that's you in round 3, exactly as you predicted.
